title: Agent and app management: who can use which Teams app or agent?
summary: The documented controls, licensing requirements and limits are supported by Microsoft Learn. The page correctly reports conflicting Microsoft guidance rather than choosing a side, including the built-in agents routes and the IsBlocked examples. Minor corrections should flag Channel Agent's public preview status and include the Actions menu in the Facilitator setup route.

claims.claim: Teams agent and app management controls organisational access to Teams apps and agents.
claims.quote: From the Manage apps page, you can review agents and apps before allowing them, access support information, and control their availability across your organization, either per user or per app.

claims.claim: Per-app availability offers Everyone, Specific users or groups, and No one.
claims.quote: Everyone | Available to all org users, new users, and guests. ... Specific users or groups | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app. ... No one | Not available to any user

claims.where: What it is: app centric management
claims.claim: Microsoft calls per-app access management app centric management, which replaces app permission policies.
claims.quote: Use the feature if already auto-migrated or manually migrate to app centric management. It replaces app permission policies.

claims.where: What it is: app permission policies
claims.claim: Microsoft describes the previous app permission policies as deprecated.
claims.quote: The previous App permission policies is deprecated.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings have separate settings for Microsoft, third-party and custom apps.
claims.quote: Under Microsoft apps, a single control automatically enables users to install and use any available agents and apps by default. ... Under Third-party apps ... Under Custom apps

claims.claim: Org-wide app defaults apply to new apps and existing apps whose availability has not been actively managed.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings apply to: All the new apps made available in Teams app store. All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.claim: Allow or Block controls whether an individual app or agent is allowed in the organisation.
claims.quote: You can allow or block specific agents and apps on either the Manage apps page or in the app details page.

claims.claim: Availability determines which users and groups can use each app or agent.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis.

claims.claim: Microsoft says all relevant access settings must allow an app or agent, while any one can block it.
claims.quote: To allow an agent or app, you must do all of the following settings. To block an agent or app, use any one of the following settings:

claims.where: summary; What it is: Unified management
claims.claim: After unification, org-wide setting changes synchronise between the Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centres in both directions.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.claim: After unification, app status changes synchronise between both admin centres.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.claim: After unification, app availability and user assignments synchronise between both admin centres.
claims.quote: Ensures consistent and synchronized agent and app behavior across platforms, as changes to app availability settings in one admin center are automatically synced with the other

claims.claim: Unified management governs app availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft Copilot apps.
claims.quote: Ensures org-wide defaults for both admin centers are in sync and governs app availability across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft Copilot apps

claims.claim: Tenants that never modified these org-wide, availability or block settings in either centre are unified automatically.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.claim: Tenants with modified settings can opt into unification through the Manage apps experience.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.where: What it is: Built-in Teams agents
claims.claim: The Manage apps overview directs Channel Agent, Facilitator and other built-in agents to their own page rather than Manage apps.
claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator, and other built-in agents available across chats, channels, and meetings are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page, not the Manage apps page.

claims.where: What it is: Facilitator setup route
claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page still gives Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.
claims.fix: Replace the attributed Facilitator setup route with 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Actions > Allow or Block'. Keep the existing explanation that the Manage apps overview gives a different route.

claims.where: What it is: Channel Agent setup route
claims.claim: The Channel Agent setup page gives Teams apps > Manage apps > Channel Agent > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: The following feature is currently in public preview. ... In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Channel Agent from the app list. ... In the Actions menu, select Allow or Block
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The Channel Agent setup page, which marks Channel Agent as public preview, likewise directs administrators to Teams apps > Manage apps > Channel Agent > Actions > Allow or Block.' Keep its existing link.

claims.claim: For new organisations, the documented default lets users install apps.
claims.quote: For new organizations, the default setting is set to let users install apps by default.

claims.claim: New third-party apps inherit the org-wide third-party availability setting rather than requiring an individual availability decision.
claims.quote: After migrating to app-centric management, a single control now manages bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps. Toggle on to enable all new and existing third-party apps across the tenant; toggle off to disable all. App-level settings stay intact.

claims.claim: The Manage apps, app centric management and unified management pages document no licence or meter for the management settings themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams app centric management unified app management licensing management settings meter. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-apps, /app-centric-management and /uam-tac-mac; none specifies a separate licence or meter for these settings.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Teams Administrator role is the documented role for using the Teams admin centre.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each organisational user needs a Teams licence before using Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Service licences for paid third-party apps can be purchased on Manage apps.
claims.quote: You can purchase licenses for services offered by third-party apps from the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Credit cards are a documented app purchasing payment method.
claims.quote: You can purchase apps using a credit card, debit card, or with invoice billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Debit cards are a documented app purchasing payment method.
claims.quote: You can purchase apps using a credit card, debit card, or with invoice billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Invoice billing is a documented app purchasing payment option.
claims.quote: Invoice billing is available as a payment option for some transactions.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Paid third-party apps
claims.claim: Plans and pricing are shown on the app details page in the Teams admin centre.
claims.quote: Select Purchase on the Manage apps page to open the Plans and pricing tab on the app details page. You can review the plans and pricing information available in admin center.

claims.claim: Invoice billing requires an admin account with both Teams Administrator and Billing Administrator roles.
claims.quote: Invoice billing is only available for an admin account that has Teams Administrator and Billing Administrator role.

claims.claim: Show tailored apps applies the tailored frontline experience to users with an F licence.
claims.quote: Under Tailored apps, turn off or turn on Show tailored apps. When this setting is on, users with an F license get the tailored frontline agent and app experience.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing: Agent package API
claims.claim: The Package Management API used to block an agent requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: In rare cases, availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Migration is one-way
claims.claim: Permission policies cannot be accessed, edited or used after moving to app centric management.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Migration is one-way
claims.claim: Migration to app centric management cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Org-wide settings skip managed apps; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide availability changes do not override individually saved app availability assignments.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you. All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually. Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Everyone availability includes guests.
claims.quote: Everyone | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: Guests cannot use an app set to Specific users or groups, even if assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conflicting policies on auto-migration
claims.claim: The limitations section says a custom-policy block conflicting with a Global-policy allow migrates the app as available to all tenant users.
claims.quote: There's no change of app permissions during the migration, except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy. Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conflicting policies on auto-migration
claims.claim: That limitations section gives available to none as the conflict outcome for EDU customers.
claims.quote: except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conflicting policies on auto-migration
claims.claim: The same page's auto-migration explanation instead describes the conflicting app as allowed for the affected user.
claims.quote: If a user is assigned to a custom app permission policy that blocks an app, while the Global permission policy allows the same app, Microsoft auto-migrates the app as allowed for that user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conflicting policies on auto-migration
claims.claim: The auto-migration explanation also describes policy-specific security groups.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy. All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Two admin centres out of step
claims.claim: Before unification, Microsoft instructs admins to keep blocked apps and org-wide settings synchronised in both centres.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Two admin centres out of step
claims.claim: Before unification, an Integrated apps block affects Outlook and Microsoft Copilot rather than Teams.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook. Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center

claims.where: Risks and limits: Bulk edits need PowerShell
claims.claim: The Teams admin centre cannot update app availability in bulk.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Bulk edits need PowerShell
claims.claim: PowerShell can update app availability in bulk.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell. For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Bulk edits need PowerShell
claims.claim: Up to 99 users or groups can be added to an app at a time.
claims.quote: You can add up to 99 users or groups at a time to an app.

claims.claim: Admins can view and manage only apps deployed in the tenant's release channel.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage agents and apps that are deployed in the same release channel as your tenant is.

claims.claim: Third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: Enabling app purchasing also enables in-app purchasing.
claims.quote: When you enable app purchasing, it also turns on in-app purchasing.

claims.claim: Blocking the app prevents users from making its in-app purchases.
claims.quote: To prevent users from making in-app purchases, you can block the app.

claims.claim: Only a Global admin can consent to unification and apply its final changes.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Teams or Global admins can prepare unification changes up to Review summary.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.claim: The cited Integrated apps controls are available to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.claim: Built-in Teams agents are no longer governed by the Microsoft apps org-wide setting.
claims.quote: These agents are no longer controlled by the Microsoft apps setting. You now manage them from the dedicated Built-in Teams agents page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents using MSCommerce PowerShell to disable third-party app purchases for users.
claims.quote: To prevent users from purchasing third-party apps, you can disable purchases using the MSCommerce PowerShell module.

claims.claim: The Usage reports page offers a Teams app usage report.
claims.quote: The Teams agent and app usage report provides information about which agents and apps in use, active users, and other usage information. | Usage reports | Teams app usage report

claims.claim: The Teams admin centre can export the app catalogue as CSV.
claims.quote: Export agent and app catalog as CSV ... As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Get-AllM365TeamsApps returns each app's status and availability.
claims.quote: Get-AllM365TeamsApps retrieves a complete list of all Teams apps in an organization, their statuses, and their availability information.

claims.claim: Get-AllM365TeamsApps identifies the last user who updated an app's availability assignment.
claims.quote: AvailableTo ... AssignedBy: UserID of the last user who updated the app available to value.

claims.claim: Per-app availability is reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group-ids> adds group availability assignments.
claims.quote: -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -AppAssignmentType: App availability type. -Groups: List of all the groups for whom the app is enabled or disabled. -OperationType: Operation performed on the app assigment. ... Add ... Remove

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType also accepts Everyone and Noone.
claims.quote: -AppAssignmentType ... Parameter sets ... (Everyone ... UsersandGroups ... Noone)

claims.claim: An app can be allowed or blocked through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked $true is a documented app-state operation, with the reference's stated direction explicitly caveated in the row.
claims.quote: PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: The reference examples describe IsBlocked $true as unblocking, while its parameter description calls it the app's state.
claims.quote: Example 3 ... -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: Org-wide app defaults are reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. You can then configure the settings in the pane.

claims.claim: No equivalent automation call is established for these per-app-type availability defaults because the documented tenant setting names are not mapped to them.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide app settings PowerShell Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings GlobalApp DefaultApp PrivateApp mapping; Org-wide app settings GlobalApp PowerShell. Read both UnifiedTenantSettings references. CustomApp search result governs uploads, not availability defaults.

claims.claim: Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings documents a GlobalApp tenant setting.
claims.quote: Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings -SettingName GlobalApp -SettingValue None ... Updates the tenant setting for GlobalApp to None

claims.claim: Built-in agent availability is reached through Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents. To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group-ids> is the documented app-centric group-assignment operation used for built-in agents.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page explicitly points to app centric management for assigning users.
claims.quote: You can also use app centric management to allow and block, create policies, and assign users. ... to assign the policy to users using app-centric management.

claims.claim: Channel Agent availability can likewise be assigned through app centric management.
claims.quote: You can also use app centric management to allow and block, create policies, and assign users. ... Follow the instructions at Add or modify app availability for users to assign the policy to users using app-centric management.

claims.claim: The unification experience starts at Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Open questions: move to unified management
claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation to move a tenant to unified management is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams unified app management PowerShell migration; Teams unified app management API move. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac and Teams PowerShell release-note excerpts. No unification-consent or migration operation found.

claims.claim: Organisation-wide agent blocking is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The package block API is in beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The package block API requires delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available. ... Application | Not available. | Not available.

claims.claim: The Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings reference lists DefaultApp, GlobalApp, PrivateApp and EnableCopilotExtensibility without mapping them to the named Org-wide app settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide app settings PowerShell Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings GlobalApp DefaultApp PrivateApp EnableCopilotExtensibility mapping. Read learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365unifiedtenantsettings; no UI mapping is given.
